reflection_text.2:
The question restricts the inventory to Knowledge = JTB and Belief as residual, so every non-K state is forced into B. With J and T independently variable we have four cells J T, J ¬T, ¬J T, ¬J ¬T. JTB identifies only J T B with Knowledge; J ¬T B, ¬J T B and ¬J ¬T B all collapse into mere Belief.

The dominant convergence in round 0 is that this coarse-graining erases two independently interesting non-knowledge cells:

* Justified false belief, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it fails truth, so with only K/B it must be counted as mere Belief. A rationally well grounded false belief is therefore indistinguishable from an arbitrary/unjustified false belief. The epistemic value of justification is invisible once truth is absent; justified falsity has no distinct home.

* Unjustified true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it fails justification, so with only K/B it must be counted as mere Belief. A lucky/accidental true belief is therefore indistinguishable from justified false belief and from unjustified false belief. The alethic value of truth is invisible once justification is absent; lucky truth has no distinct home.

Hence Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B, losing independent tracking of justification and truth. This is described variously as the justification gap / truth gap and as the independence problem of J and T.

A related formal pressure noted by colleagues 10-11 is how J itself can be cashed out on a B/K only inventory. Cashed out by further beliefs it yields an infinite regress of justifiers; cashed out by knowledge it makes J(p) depend on K(q) which itself contains a belief in need of justification, yielding circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational stop. That regress/circularity is presented as the formal expression of the coarse-graining.

Disagreement/variation: colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 frame the problem as circular truth-verification and non-arbitrary justification standards that cannot be reduced to B/K without external criteria. Colleagues 10-11 foreground regress/circularity, colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 foreground the loss of distinct states for justified false belief and unjustified true belief. The two accounts are compatible: the loss of distinct states is the taxonomy effect of the regress/circularity constraint.

Current belief: the two core non-Gettier problems under a strict K/B inventory are the disappearance of a state for justified false belief and the disappearance of a state for unjustified true belief, i.e. the inability to keep apart epistemic virtue of justification from truth absence and truth presence from justification absence. Whether to phrase that as regress/circularity of justification or as coarse-graining is a matter of presentation; the content is the same.

Unresolved: how much weight to give to the explicit regress vs circularity formulation versus the taxonomy coarse-graining formulation when the final answer is required; and whether the question expects regress/circularity as the two problems rather than the two collapsed cells.
reflection_text.3:
The discussion centers on what is lost when the epistemic inventory is restricted to Knowledge = Justified True Belief and the residual category Belief.

There is broad agreement that with only K and B the 2×2 truth × justification matrix collapses: JTB → K, and ¬K → B. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B.

The dominant formulation repeated by Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 is the coarse-graining / independence loss:
* Justified false belief. J∧¬T∧B is not Knowledge because it is false, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must be counted as mere Belief. Justified falsity is lumped with unjustified falsity; the epistemic merit of justification is erased once truth fails.
* Unjustified true belief. ¬J∧T∧B is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so it must also be counted as mere Belief. A lucky/accidental true belief is lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief; the alethic merit of truth is erased once justification fails.

Hence the taxonomy cannot mark off a justified belief that is false as a sui generis rational-but-false state, nor a true belief that is unjustified as a sui generis lucky-but-unwarranted state. Knowledge is too narrow and Belief is too broad.

A second, linked line stresses the internal grounding of the J-clause given the same inventory. Colleagues 10,11 note that justification of p has to be cashed out in the only available states, belief or knowledge.
* If J(p) is cashed out by a further belief B(q), J(q) is required, etc., giving the familiar regress of justification with no non-infinite B-chain to ground p.
* If the chain is stopped by making the justifier itself a knowledge state K(q), K(q) is B(q)&T(q)&J(q), so justification of p depends on justification of q and you are back in regress, or else you close the chain dogmatically/foundationally with an unjustified basic belief/knowledge.

Colleagues 1,5,7,9,14,13 phrase this as the need for an external/non-epistemic criterion for truth and for a non-arbitrary standard for justification, and as circularity in verifying truth without already presupposing knowledge. That is the formal expression of the coarse-graining: justification and truth cannot be independently tracked in a two-state taxonomy, so J either regresses or is stipulated.

Unresolved tension: some colleagues present the regress/circularity as the primary problem, others present the JFB/UTB indistinguishability as the primary problem. They appear interdependent: the lack of an independent justified-belief state is what forces the regress/dogmatism dilemma and what makes Belief a heterogeneous dump.

I am keeping both the justification-gap / truth-gap collapse of JFB and UTB into bare Belief, and the regress/circularity/dogmatism problem for cashing out J in terms of only B/K, as the two closely linked non-Gettier difficulties under the K/B restriction.
reflection_text.6:
The round-0 discussion clusters around the consequence of forcing the four J×T combinations into only the two boxes Knowledge = J∧T∧B and Belief = ¬Knowledge.

A strong majority — Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 — frames the problem as coarse-graining / loss of independence of justification and truth. With only K/B available, every non-K state is lumped into Belief:
* J∧¬T∧B = justified false belief must be called mere Belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails; justified falsity is indistinguishable from unjustified falsity.
* ¬J∧T∧B = unjustified true belief must also be called mere Belief. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails; lucky/accidental true belief is indistinguishable from false belief and from justified false belief.

Belief therefore becomes the heterogeneous disjunction J&~T&B ∨ ~J&T&B ∨ ~J&~T&B, so the taxonomy cannot mark off a justified but false state nor a true but unjustified state. This is described as the justification gap and the truth gap, the independence problem of J and T distinct from Gettier.

A second strand — Colleagues 10,11,1,7,5,9,14 — reformulates the same inventory limit meta-epistemically:
* Justification cannot be cashed out in the allowed vocabulary. If J(p) is to be a further epistemic state it must be B(q) or K(q). B(q) requires J(q) → regress of justification; stopping the regress with K(q) re-introduces J(q) and yields circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational belief.
* Truth cannot be independently verified from within the K/B inventory without smuggling in an external criterion, so truth-checking risks collapsing into further belief/knowledge attributions.

These meta-epistemic worries are essentially the regress/circularity version of the coarse-graining worry: with no distinct justified-belief state, justification has nowhere to be realized except via more beliefs/knowledge.

Disagreement / nuance noted:
* Some colleagues stress regress/circularity and truth verification as the two problems; others stress the two missing cells justified false belief and unjustified true belief.
* Colleagues 13,14,5,7 also mention circular truth assessment and arbitrary justification standards, which overlap with the regress point.

Current working understanding: The inventory limit makes Belief a grab-bag and removes an epistemic place for justified false belief and for unjustified true belief. That is the core non-Gettier difficulty; the regress/circularity formulation is the formal expression of the same limitation. Unresolved is whether the examiner wants the formulation in terms of the two missing cells or in terms of justification regress + truth verification.
reflection_text.8:
The discussion is split between a regress/circularity diagnosis and a taxonomy-coarsening diagnosis, both stemming from the restriction to only Knowledge and Belief as epistemic states.

With K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p) and only K/B available, every non-K state must be classified as mere Belief. That forces Belief to be heterogeneous: J&T&B = K; J&~T&B, ~J&T&B, ~J&~T&B all = Belief.

The dominant coarse-graining claim, made by Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12:
1. Justified false belief problem / justification gap. A belief can be properly justified yet false. JTB makes it non-K, so on a K/B only scheme it is forced into Belief, lumped with unjustified false belief. The epistemic merit of justification is invisible once truth fails; there is no distinct state for ‘justified but false’.
2. Unjustified true belief problem / truth gap. A belief can be true by luck/accident with no justification. JTB makes it non-K, so it is also forced into Belief, lumped with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. The alethic merit of truth is invisible once justification fails; there is no distinct state for ‘true but unwarranted’.

Hence Belief becomes J&~T&B ∨ ~J&T&B ∨ ~J&~T&B, and justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of the K/B dichotomy.

A minority strand, Colleagues 1,10,11,13,14,7,9, argues the same restriction makes justification uncashable in K/B terms. If J(p) must be given by another epistemic state, either a further belief B(q) requiring J(q) → infinite regress of justification, or a knowledge state K(q) which itself contains B(q) & J(q) → circularity/dogmatism. This is presented as the formal expression of the coarse-graining: no independent justified-belief state to stop the chain, so justification is either circular or foundational/dogmatic.

Unresolved tension: whether the two problems should be framed as the regress/circularity of justification and the non-verifiability of truth within K/B, or as the concrete loss of distinct epistemic places for justified false belief and unjustified true belief. The latter is the operational consequence of the former under the two-state inventory, and Gettier is explicitly set aside.
reflection_text.4:
The discussion is about JTB with only two epistemic kinds, Knowledge = B & T & J and Belief as the residual category. 

Consensus majority: with only K/B the 2x2 justification x truth matrix collapses into K = J∧T∧B and Belief = ¬K. Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous dump of J∧¬T∧B, ¬J∧T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B.

The two taxonomic losses repeatedly named are:

* Justified false belief. A belief can be properly justified and still false. JTB makes it non-knowledge because T fails, so on a K/B only scheme it is forced into mere Belief, lumped with unjustified false belief. The epistemic value of justification is erased when truth is absent; there is no state for ‘justified but wrong’.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by luck/accident with no justification. JTB makes it non-knowledge because J fails, so on a K/B only scheme it is forced into mere Belief, lumped with justified false belief and unjustified false belief. The alethic value of truth is erased when justification is absent; lucky true belief is indiscriminable from false belief.

Several colleagues frame the same difficulty as a justification grounding problem: Jp must be cashed out in epistemic terms. With only B and K as states, J can only be a further belief or a knowledge. That yields a regress of B justifiers, or if stopped by K, circularity/dogmatism because K already contains J. This regress/circularity is presented as the formal expression of the coarse-graining.

Divergence to note: Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 emphasize regress/circularity and an external non-epistemic criterion needed to verify truth/justification, i.e. truth cannot be verified internally to B/K and justification standards risk arbitrariness. The dominant thread from colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12 is the loss of distinct states for justified false belief and unjustified true belief.

Unresolved for me: whether the intended “two problems” are the two missing cells J¬T and ¬JT, or the regress/circularity vs coarse-graining pair. The taxonomic loss appears to be the direct consequence of the regress/circularity constraint, so they may be two descriptions of the same issue. Gettier is to be ignored.

Current leaning: the core non-Gettier difficulty under a strict K/B inventory is the inability to keep justification and truth independently trackable, i.e. the justified-false and true-unjustified problems, with regress/circularity as the mechanism that forces the collapse.
reflection_text.10:
The question is about the JTB analysis under a strict K/B inventory, Gettier set aside. The public round is heavily convergent on a coarse-graining / loss of independent tracking of J and T.

Consensus core: With K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p) and only K and B as attitude kinds, every non-K state is forced into B. That makes Belief a heterogeneous residue:
J & T & B = K
J & ~T & B , ~J & T & B , ~J & ~T & B = Belief

Hence J and T can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class.

Dominant two-cell objection:
1. Justified false belief. A belief can be properly justified and still false. On JTB it is not K because ~T, so with only K/B it must be counted as mere Belief. Justified falsity is therefore lumped with unjustified falsity; the epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails. Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 explicitly name this as the justification gap / justified-but-wrong problem.
2. Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by luck/accident with no justification. On JTB it is not K because ~J, so with only K/B it must be counted as mere Belief. Accidentally true belief is therefore lumped with justified false belief and with plain false belief; the alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails. Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 explicitly name this as the truth gap / lucky-true problem.

This gives Belief = J&~T&B ∨ ~J&T&B ∨ ~J&~T&B, a non-uniform grab bag, and no place to mark warranted error vs unwarranted error, or lucky truth vs warranted truth.

A secondary strand in the discussion is the metajustificatory regress/circularity worry: J(p) has to be cashed out in epistemic terms, but with only B and K available justification either regresses through ever further beliefs, or is stopped dogmatically by making the justifier itself a K state, which already contains J, leading to circularity. Colleagues 10,11,7,14,5,9 emphasize this. It is compatible with the coarse-graining point: the lack of an independent justified-belief state is what forces the regress/dogmatism dilemma.

I am keeping both strands, but the inventory constraint makes the collapse of JFB and UTB into mere Belief the most direct formal problem, with the regress/circularity as the formal expression of why justification cannot be given an independent state in a two-state taxonomy. Unresolved: whether the intended “two problems” are the two collapse cases JFB and UTB, or the regress vs truth-verification circularity pair. The majority textual weight in round 0 favors JFB and UTB.
reflection_text.11:
The discussion centers on the collapse that occurs when the epistemic inventory is restricted to Knowledge and Belief only, with K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p).

With only K and B available, every attitude that is not K must be placed under B. That makes Belief a heterogeneous residual disjunction: J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B.

The dominant strand in round 0 is the coarse-graining / independence loss:
* Justified false belief. J & ¬T & B is not K because K is factive. On a K/B only scheme it is forced into mere Belief, so a properly justified but false belief is lumped with unjustified false belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is invisible once truth fails. Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12, etc., call this the justification gap / ‘justified but wrong’ problem.
* Unjustified true belief. ¬J & T & B is not K because K requires justification. On a K/B only scheme it is also forced into mere Belief, so a lucky/accidental true belief is lumped with false beliefs and with justified false beliefs. The alethic virtue of truth is invisible once justification fails. This is the truth gap / ‘lucky truth’ problem.

Several colleagues frame the same pressure as a regress / circularity problem for the J-clause. With no distinct justified-belief state, J(p) must be cashed out in the only states available, B or K. If J is cashed out by a further belief B(q), J(q) is then required, etc., giving an infinite regress; if the regress is stopped by K(q), K(q) itself contains B(q)&T(q)&J(q), so justification of p depends on justification of q, leading to circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary basic belief/knowledge stop. Colleagues 10,11,7,14 highlight this.

Noted disagreements/nuances:
- Some present regress/circularity as the primary problem, others present the loss of justified false belief and unjustified true belief as the primary problem. They are inter-related: the lack of an independent justified-belief state is what forces the regress and the coarse-graining.
- Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 also mention the difficulty of verifying truth and specifying a non-arbitrary justification standard from within K/B only, which is a variant of the same grounding worry.

Unresolved for me: whether the question wants the two distinct state-collapse cases, or the two justificatory structural problems of regress vs dogmatism/circularity. The evidence so far points most strongly to the pair: no epistemic place for justified false belief, and no epistemic place for unjustified true belief, i.e. truth and justification cannot be tracked independently of the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy. The regress/circularity diagnosis is the formal expression of that same limitation.

Current working understanding: JTB with only K/B forces Belief to do duty for both J&¬T and ¬J&T, erasing the independent normative value of justification and truth, and because justification must be expressed in B/K terms it cannot be grounded non-circularly without infinite regress or dogmatic foundations. Gettier is set aside.
reflection_text.12:
The discussion so far converges on the coarse-graining that follows from restricting the epistemic inventory to Knowledge = J ∧ T ∧ B and Belief as the sole residual category.

With only K and B the 2×2 J×T matrix collapses:
* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B, ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B all = Belief

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous disjunction. The loss of independent tracking of justification and truth is repeatedly described as a justification-gap/truth-gap and as a regress/circularity problem for the J-clause.

Most of the strongest consensus is around two non-Gettier cells that become indistinguishable from plain, unwarranted false belief:

1. Justified false belief, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it fails the truth condition, so with a K/B only taxonomy it must be counted as mere Belief. A rationally warranted but false belief is therefore lumped with unjustified false belief; the epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth is absent. This is the “justified but wrong / false lemma” difficulty.

2. Unjustified true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it fails the justification condition, so it too must be counted as mere Belief. A lucky/accidental true belief is therefore lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief; the alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification is absent. This is the “lucky guess / true without warrant” difficulty.

Colleagues 10,11 also stress the formal expression of the coarse-graining: because Jp must be cashed out in the only available states, Jp can only be a belief or a knowledge. If Jp is a belief you get a regress of justification, B(q) needing J(q) needing...; if Jp is made to rest on K(q) you get circularity/dogmatism, since K(q) already contains a belief that needs a justifier, and the only way to stop the chain is an arbitrary basic belief/knowledge. Truth verification is likewise said to require a prior epistemic grip that is not supplied by K/B alone.

Disagreement in emphasis: Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 frame the problem primarily as the loss of JFB and UTB as distinct epistemic states; Colleagues 1,10,11,5,7,9,14 frame it as regress/circularity of justification and the inability to verify truth non-circularly from within K/B. The two framings are compatible: the regress/circularity is the formal consequence of having no independent justified-belief state to realise justification, and the JFB/UTB collapse is the observable taxonomy consequence.

Unresolved / to keep: whether the question wants the regress/circularity formulation or the JFB/UTB coarse-graining formulation as the “two problems”. Current evidence favors JFB and UTB as the two canonical non-Gettier problems under a binary K/B inventory, with regress/circularity as the underlying justification problem.

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The dominant line of argument so far has already isolated the core difficulty very cleanly. With only Knowledge and Belief on the table, JTB forces the four cells of the justification-by-truth matrix (J∧T, J∧¬T, ¬J∧T, ¬J∧¬T) into just two categories. That immediately erases any distinct home for justified false belief and for unjustified true belief; both must be dumped into the single residual label “Belief.” The result is that Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all that conflates epistemically responsible error with epistemically irresponsible truth, and the JTB analysis loses any capacity to mark the independent normative contributions of justification and truth. Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 have each spelled this out in slightly different but mutually reinforcing terms, and the 2×2 grid language makes the coarseness especially vivid. Until we are given a third primitive state (for instance, something like “justified belief” that is neutral on truth), the collapse is unavoidable and the two problems remain exactly those two gaps.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 10 and 11 rightly note that justification must be cashed out in one of the two allowed states, but that observation actually sharpens rather than displaces the deeper taxonomy problem. Once J is forced back into either B or K, the only remaining distinction the framework can draw is K versus everything else; this immediately collapses the four cells of the J/T matrix into two, so that both justified false belief and unjustified true belief become indistinguishable from plain unjustified false belief. That loss of independent tracking for justification and truth is the primary defect the JTB analysis exhibits under the given constraint, and it is what renders the regress/circularity dilemma secondary: the dilemma only arises because the framework has already erased any intermediate state in which justification could be marked without collapsing into the same two bins. The resulting heterogeneous “Belief” category therefore erases precisely the epistemic differences that JTB was meant to preserve, even before any chain of justifiers is considered.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 10 and 11 rightly flag the regress/circularity worry that arises once justification must be cashed out in the only two available states, yet that worry is derivative rather than fundamental. It surfaces only if one insists on an internalist, belief-to-belief chain; externalist or foundational stops can truncate the chain without contradiction. What remains primary, even after such stops are allowed, is the resulting taxonomy: once every non-K state is forced into the single residual category Belief, we lose any way to mark off justified false belief from unjustified false belief (the justification gap) and unjustified true belief from justified false belief (the truth gap). That collapse is visible in the responses of colleagues 2–4, 6, 8 and 12, and it persists independently of whether the regress is blocked. A hybrid formulation therefore seems most accurate: JTB under a strict K/B inventory both erases those two distinctions and, when pressed for an independent truth check, either imports an external criterion or collapses back into the same heterogeneous Belief. This accounts for the coarseness that survives even after Gettier cases are set aside.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The strongest case emerging across the group is that the two core problems are precisely the forced collapse of justified false belief into the same residual category as unjustified false belief, and the collapse of unjustified true belief into the same residual category as justified false belief. Once only Knowledge and Belief remain available, every non-KTB state must be labeled Belief, erasing any independent tracking of justification when truth fails and of truth when justification fails. This is not merely a side effect; it is the direct consequence of the JTB schema under a two-state restriction, and it leaves the taxonomy unable to mark the epistemic merit of a well-supported falsehood or the epistemic defect of a lucky truth. The regress and circularity worries that some colleagues have raised appear downstream of this coarsening: they arise only once one tries to cash out justification using the very same depleted inventory of states. Externalist or foundational stipulations can block an actual regress in practice, but they cannot restore the lost distinctions inside the JTB framework itself. The JFB/UTB heterogeneity therefore remains the primary defect even after Gettier cases are set aside.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 10 and 11 make a strong formal case for regress and circularity once J is forced into the K/B dichotomy, but that framing treats the justification clause as an independent primitive that can still be analyzed on its own. Once we accept the coarser taxonomy that the question imposes—only K and B as available states—the more immediate and structural problems are the two that most of the group has already identified: the forced heterogeneity of the Belief category and the resulting inability to track justification and truth independently. 

Any justified false belief must be dumped into plain Belief alongside unjustified false beliefs, erasing the epistemic merit of justification when truth fails; likewise any unjustified true belief is indistinguishable from every other non-knowledge case, erasing the alethic merit of truth when justification fails. These are not downstream consequences of an attempted regress; they are the direct result of collapsing the four J/T combinations into a single residual label. Regress worries only surface if one still tries to cash J out inside that already-collapsed space; the taxonomy itself has already lost the distinctions needed to make JTB do its intended work. The independence gaps between justification and truth therefore remain the two core difficulties even before any chain of further beliefs is considered.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 4's 2x2 framing, echoed by 6 and 8, captures the core difficulty most cleanly. With only Knowledge and Belief available, the four cells of the justification/truth matrix are collapsed so that J∧¬T∧B, ¬J∧T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B are all forced into the single residual label "Belief." That erases any independent tracking of justification when truth fails and of truth when justification fails; a justified false belief is thereby treated as no better than an irrational one, and an unjustified true belief is treated as no better than a false one. The taxonomy therefore cannot mark the normative difference between epistemic virtue and epistemic luck even before any regress arises.

The regress/circularity concern raised by 10 and 11 is real but not distinctive to JTB under the two-state constraint; it is simply the familiar foundationalist stopping problem that externalist or basic-belief moves are routinely invoked to block in other contexts. What remains peculiar to the present restriction is the forced heterogeneity of Belief itself: the label must now serve simultaneously as the home for epistemically good-but-false states and for epistemically defective-but-true states. That loss of discrimination is what renders the JTB analysis inadequate once the inventory is limited to Knowledge and Belief.

2.text:
With only K and B as the live categories JTB forces a 2x2 J x T matrix into a
binary K / not-K partition.

K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p)
not-K(p) := B(p) & [¬T(p) ∨ ¬J(p)]

Hence every non-knowledge state is dumped into the residual class Belief.
Belief is therefore the heterogeneous disjunction

B ≡ J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B

and justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of the
knowledge/belief dichotomy.

That coarse graining erases two epistemically distinct non-knowledge cells.

* The justification gap / justified false belief. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not
knowledge because JTB is factive, so on a K/B inventory it must be called
mere Belief. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore
indistinguishable from an arbitrary unjustified false belief. The epistemic
value of justification disappears once truth is absent; there is no state
for ‘justified but wrong’.

* The truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge
because JTB is justification dependent, so on a K/B inventory it must also
be called mere Belief. A true belief that is lucky, accidental or blindly
guessed is therefore indistinguishable from justified false belief and from
unjustified false belief. The alethic value of truth disappears once
justification is absent; there is no state for ‘true but unwarranted’.

In inventory terms Belief has to be both justified and unjustified and both
true and false at once. Knowledge is made too narrow because it excludes
justified false beliefs we want to count as epistemically good, and Belief
is made too broad because it conflates lucky true beliefs with bad false
beliefs and justified false beliefs with unjustified false beliefs.

That is the formal expression of the regress/circularity pressure on J.
Cashed out in the only available states, J(p) must be a further B(q) or
K(q).  J(p) via B(q) gives an infinite regress of beliefs each in need of a
justifier; J(p) via K(q) makes justification depend on a state that already
contains a belief in need of justification, i.e. circularity/dogmatism or an
arbitrary foundational stop. The regress/circularity dilemma is just the
formal way the K/B coarse-graining makes justification unstatable as an
independent epistemic condition, leaving the two lost cells justified false
belief and unjustified true belief with no distinct home.

3.text:
With only Knowledge = J & T & B and the residual category Belief the 2×2 truth × justification matrix is coarse-grained to

K = J∧T∧B
B = J∧¬T∧B  ∨  ¬J∧T∧B  ∨  ¬J∧¬T∧B

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of the K/B dichotomy. Knowledge is too narrow and Belief is a heterogeneous dump.

* The justification gap / justified false belief. A belief can be properly justified and still false. JTB is factive so J∧¬T∧B is not Knowledge, and with only K/B it must be counted as mere Belief. A justified but false belief is therefore lumped together with unjustified false belief and, more generally, with all ¬K. The epistemic merit of justification is erased once truth fails; we have no epistemic place for a sui generis rational-but-false state, i.e. no distinct justified-belief state.

* The truth gap / unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by luck, accident or guesswork and yet wholly unjustified. JTB is justification-dependent so ¬J∧T∧B is not Knowledge, and with only K/B it must also be counted as mere Belief. A lucky true belief is therefore lumped together with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic merit of truth is erased once justification fails; we have no epistemic place for a sui generis true-but-unwarranted state, i.e. no distinct true-belief state.

That coarse-graining is the formal expression of the justification problem under a K/B only inventory. J(p) has to be cashed out in the only available states. Caching it out in B(q) gives the familiar regress J(p) → B(q) → J(q) → …, and closing the chain with K(q) re-introduces J(q) so the regress is reproduced, or else it is stopped by an arbitrary, unjustified basic belief/knowledge, i.e. dogmatism/circularity. In practice J and T cannot be independently marked: Belief has to be both justified and unjustified and both true and false at once.

4.text:
With K = B & T & J and B as the only residual class the 2x2 J x T
space has to be coarse-grained to

K = J ∧ T ∧ B
B = ¬K = J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of the
Knowledge/Belief dichotomy. Belief becomes a heterogeneous dump and
two epistemically distinct non-knowledge cells disappear.

* The justification gap / justified false belief. 
A belief can be properly justified and yet false, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. On JTB
that is not knowledge because T fails. With only K/B as states it is
forced into mere Belief and is therefore lumped together with
¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. The epistemic virtue of being justified
is erased when truth is absent: a rational, well grounded false belief
is indiscriminable from an arbitrary, unjustified false belief. In
taxonomic terms there is no state for ‘justified but wrong’.

* The truth gap / unjustified true belief.
A belief can be true by luck, accident or blind guess with no
justification at all, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. On JTB that is not knowledge because
J fails. With only K/B as states it is forced into mere Belief and is
therefore lumped together with J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The
alethic value of truth is erased when justification is absent: a lucky
true belief is indiscriminable from a justified false belief and from
an unjustified false belief. In taxonomic terms there is no state for
‘true but unwarranted’.

That coarse graining is the formal expression of the justification
problem on a K/B only inventory. Jp can only be cashed out in
epistemic terms as a further B or a further K. Cashed out by belief
you get the regress of justification: every justifier is itself a belief
in need of a justifier. Stopped by knowledge you get
K(p) iff K(p) is true and Bp, i.e. circularity/dogmatism, because
K(q) already contains B(q) which itself needs a justifier. The
regress/circularity dilemma is just what forces J and T to be
invisible inside the single residual class Belief, so justified false
belief and unjustified true belief have no independent home in the
theory. Gettier aside this is the classic truth-versus-justification
pressure on the tripartite analysis.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:

With K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p) and only the two attitude labels K and B available, B has to be the residual class ¬K. That makes B heterogeneous and it erases the independent normative work that J and T are supposed to do.

On a K/B only taxonomy:

* J & T & B = K
* J & ¬T & B = B
* ¬J & T & B = B
* ¬J & ¬T & B = B

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked separately from the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy.

1. The justification gap – justified false belief has no home. 
A belief can be properly justified and still be false; JTB is factive so it is not K. With only K/B the justified false belief J&¬T&B is forced into mere Belief and is lumped with unjustified false belief ¬J&¬T&B. The epistemic virtue of justification is invisible once truth fails: a rational, well grounded false belief is indiscriminable from an arbitrary, irrational false belief. Knowledge is thereby too narrow and Belief is made too broad.

2. The truth gap – unjustified true belief has no home. 
A belief can be true by luck, accident or blind guess with no justification at all; JTB is justification dependent so it is not K. With only K/B the unjustified true belief ¬J&T&B is forced into mere Belief and is lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is invisible once justification fails: a lucky true belief is indiscriminable from a false belief. Belief therefore conflates epistemically good justification/bad truth with bad justification/good truth.

That is the classic coarse-graining objection, distinct from Gettier. It is the formal expression of the regress/dogmatism worry colleagues 10-11 raise: J cannot be cashed out in B/K terms without making justification either regress ad infinitum through B-states or stop arbitrarily in a basic K/B, i.e. you have no independent state for “justified belief” as such. The upshot is that on a bare Knowledge/Belief inventory JTB cannot keep apart warranted error from unwarranted error, nor lucky truth from warranted truth.

6.text:
With only K = J & T & B and B = ¬K in the inventory the 2x2 J/T matrix
collapses into one positive cell and one heterogeneous residual.

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ~T B = Belief
* ~J T B = Belief
* ~J ~T B = Belief

Belief is therefore J&~T&B ∨ ~J&T&B ∨ ~J&~T&B. Justification and truth can
no longer be tracked independently of the K/B dichotomy.

1. The justification gap / justified-false-belief gap.  
A belief can be properly justified and still false. On JTB it is not
Knowledge because the truth condition fails, so on a K/B only taxonomy it
must be counted as mere Belief. Justified false belief is thereby lumped
together with unjustified false belief. The epistemic value of being
justified is erased once truth fails and there is no epistemic home for
‘justified belief as such’. Justified falsity is epistemically indiscriminable
from unjustified falsity.

2. The truth gap / unjustified-true-belief gap.  
A belief can be true by luck, accident or blind guess and yet be wholly
unjustified. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the justification condition
fails, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must again be counted as mere Belief.
Unjustified true belief is thereby lumped together with justified false
belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic value of being true is
erased once justification fails and there is no epistemic home for ‘true
belief as such’. Lucky truth is epistemically indiscriminable from false
belief.

That is the classic coarse-graining objection. In the usual formalisation
it is expressed as the fact that with no distinct justified-belief state
justification has nowhere to be realised except via further B or K states.
Cashing J(p) out by B(q) generates the regress of justification, and cashing
it out by K(q) re-introduces J(q) and so is circular or dogmatic. The
regress / circularity and the truth-verification worry are just the
meta-epistemic expression of the same inventory limit: justification cannot
be marked off from belief when truth is absent and truth cannot be marked
off from belief when justification is absent.

10.text:
With the tripartite analysis

K(p) := B(p) ∧ T(p) ∧ J(p)

and the only attitude kinds allowed in the taxonomy being Knowledge and Belief, every state that is not K is forced into the single residual class B.

That is

* J ∧ T ∧ B = K
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = Belief

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag and the
justification / truth matrix is coarse-grained to Knowledge vs not-Knowledge.

The two cells that are lost are the two non-K cells that are epistemically
distinct from plain unwarranted false belief.

1. The justification gap / justified-false-belief problem. A belief can be
properly justified and yet false. JTB is factive so J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not K.
With only K/B as states it must be counted as mere Belief, and is lumped
together with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The epistemic virtue of justification is
erased once truth fails: a well warranted false belief is
indistinguishable in the taxonomy from an arbitrary, unjustified false
belief. There is no independent state for justified belief as such.

2. The truth gap / unjustified-true-belief problem. A belief can be true
by luck, accident or blind guess with no justification at all. JTB is
justification dependent so ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not K. With only K/B as states
it must again be counted as mere Belief, and is lumped together both with
J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The alethic virtue of truth is erased
once justification fails: a lucky true belief is indistinguishable in the
taxonomy from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false
belief. There is no independent state for true belief as such.

Hence Knowledge is made too narrow – it excludes justified false beliefs
we want to count as epistemically good – and Belief is made too broad –
it conflates warranted error with unwarranted error and lucky truth with
falsehood. The loss of an independent justified-belief state is the
formal expression of why J(p) cannot be cashed out on a bare K/B
inventory without regress: J(p) has to be given in epistemic terms, so
either it regresses through ever further B-states, or it is stopped by
making the justifier itself a K-state, i.e. K(q) := B(q)&T(q)&J(q), which
already contains a belief in need of a justifier. The coarse-graining
into JFB and UTB is the direct non-Gettier pressure on the JTB
dichotomy.

8.text:
With K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p) and only K and B as live categories every
attitude that is not K is put under B.

B is then the heterogeneous residue

B ≡ J&T&B  ∨  J&~T&B  ∨  ~J&T&B  ∨  ~J&~T&B
   = K  ∨  JFB  ∨  UTB  ∨  UFB

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of the K/B
dichotomy.

* Justification gap / justified false belief. 
J&~T&B is not K because K is factive. On a K/B only inventory it has to be
counted as mere Belief. A properly justified but false belief is therefore
lumped together with unjustified false belief. The normative difference
between a rational false belief and an irrational false belief is lost and
there is no epistemic place for ‘justified belief as such’. The epistemic
merit of justification is invisible once truth fails.

* Truth gap / unjustified true belief.
~J&T&B is not K because K is justification dependent. On a K/B only
inventory it has to be counted as mere Belief. A true belief that is true
by luck, accident or guesswork is therefore lumped together with justified
false belief and unjustified false belief. The alethic merit of truth is
invisible once justification fails and there is no epistemic place for
‘true belief as such’.

In a two-state taxonomy Belief has to do duty for justified-but-false and
true-but-unjustified. Knowledge is too narrow – it excludes justified false
beliefs we want to count as epistemically good – and Belief is too broad –
it conflates lucky true beliefs with bad false beliefs and justified false
beliefs with unjustified false beliefs. 

That coarse-graining is the formal expression of the familiar
justification regress/circularity worry under the K/B restriction: J(p) has
to be cashed out in epistemic terms, i.e. in B(q) or K(q). B(q) needs J(q),
etc., giving an infinite regress of beliefs, or the chain is stopped by a
K(q) which itself contains B(q)&J(q), so justification of p depends on the
justification of q and you get circularity/dogmatism. There is no independent
justified-belief state to stop the chain, which is why the two
non-knowledge cells above have no home. Gettier aside, this is the loss of a
distinct place for justified false belief and for unjustified true belief.

12.text:
With only two labels, K and B, the JxT space is forced to coarse grain.

On JTB
K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p)

and everything else is just B. On a binary inventory

* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = Belief

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the residual category. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction of justified false, true unjustified and unjustified false belief.

That coarse graining makes two intuitively distinct non-knowledge states disappear.

1. The justification gap / justified false belief. 
J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is factive. With K/B only it must be counted as mere Belief. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore lumped with an arbitrary, unjustified false belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth is absent: justified falsity and unjustified falsity are indiscriminable as mere belief, even though the former is epistemically much better than the latter. In the taxonomy there is no place for a justified belief as such.

2. The truth gap / unjustified true belief. 
¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is justification dependent. With K/B only it must be counted as mere Belief. A lucky, accidental or blindly guessed true belief is therefore lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification is absent: accidentally true belief is indiscriminable as mere belief from false belief, even though it shares truth with knowledge and is alethically better than false belief. In the taxonomy there is no place for a true belief as such.

Hence Knowledge is too narrow and Belief is too broad. Belief has to do duty for both “justified but false” and “true but unjustified”. The formal expression of the loss is the classic regress/circularity of the J-clause on a B/K only stock: J(p) can only be cashed out by another B or K state, so J(p) either needs J(q) ad infinitum if cashed out by belief, or requires K(q) which already contains a belief needing a justifier, i.e. circularity/dogmatism. The regress/circularity is the formal consequence of having no independent justified-belief state to realise justification, and the JFB / UTB collapse is the observable taxonomy consequence.

public_text.1: The dominant line of argument so far has already isolated the core difficulty very cleanly. With only Knowledge and Belief on the table, JTB forces the four cells of the justification-by-truth matrix (J∧T, J∧¬T, ¬J∧T, ¬J∧¬T) into just two categories. That immediately erases any distinct home for justified false belief and for unjustified true belief; both must be dumped into the single residual label “Belief.” The result is that Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all that conflates epistemically responsible error with epistemically irresponsible truth, and the JTB analysis loses any capacity to mark the independent normative contributions of justification and truth. Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 have each spelled this out in slightly different but mutually reinforcing terms, and the 2×2 grid language makes the coarseness especially vivid. Until we are given a third primitive state (for instance, something like “justified belief” that is neutral on truth), the collapse is unavoidable and the two problems remain exactly those two gaps.
public_text.9: Colleagues 10 and 11 rightly note that justification must be cashed out in one of the two allowed states, but that observation actually sharpens rather than displaces the deeper taxonomy problem. Once J is forced back into either B or K, the only remaining distinction the framework can draw is K versus everything else; this immediately collapses the four cells of the J/T matrix into two, so that both justified false belief and unjustified true belief become indistinguishable from plain unjustified false belief. That loss of independent tracking for justification and truth is the primary defect the JTB analysis exhibits under the given constraint, and it is what renders the regress/circularity dilemma secondary: the dilemma only arises because the framework has already erased any intermediate state in which justification could be marked without collapsing into the same two bins. The resulting heterogeneous “Belief” category therefore erases precisely the epistemic differences that JTB was meant to preserve, even before any chain of justifiers is considered.
public_text.7: Colleagues 10 and 11 rightly flag the regress/circularity worry that arises once justification must be cashed out in the only two available states, yet that worry is derivative rather than fundamental. It surfaces only if one insists on an internalist, belief-to-belief chain; externalist or foundational stops can truncate the chain without contradiction. What remains primary, even after such stops are allowed, is the resulting taxonomy: once every non-K state is forced into the single residual category Belief, we lose any way to mark off justified false belief from unjustified false belief (the justification gap) and unjustified true belief from justified false belief (the truth gap). That collapse is visible in the responses of colleagues 2–4, 6, 8 and 12, and it persists independently of whether the regress is blocked. A hybrid formulation therefore seems most accurate: JTB under a strict K/B inventory both erases those two distinctions and, when pressed for an independent truth check, either imports an external criterion or collapses back into the same heterogeneous Belief. This accounts for the coarseness that survives even after Gettier cases are set aside.
public_text.14: The strongest case emerging across the group is that the two core problems are precisely the forced collapse of justified false belief into the same residual category as unjustified false belief, and the collapse of unjustified true belief into the same residual category as justified false belief. Once only Knowledge and Belief remain available, every non-KTB state must be labeled Belief, erasing any independent tracking of justification when truth fails and of truth when justification fails. This is not merely a side effect; it is the direct consequence of the JTB schema under a two-state restriction, and it leaves the taxonomy unable to mark the epistemic merit of a well-supported falsehood or the epistemic defect of a lucky truth. The regress and circularity worries that some colleagues have raised appear downstream of this coarsening: they arise only once one tries to cash out justification using the very same depleted inventory of states. Externalist or foundational stipulations can block an actual regress in practice, but they cannot restore the lost distinctions inside the JTB framework itself. The JFB/UTB heterogeneity therefore remains the primary defect even after Gettier cases are set aside.

With K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p) and only the two attitude labels K and B available, B has to be the residual class ¬K. That makes B heterogeneous and it erases the independent normative work that J and T are supposed to do.

On a K/B only taxonomy:

* J & T & B = K
* J & ¬T & B = B
* ¬J & T & B = B
* ¬J & ¬T & B = B

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked separately from the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy.

1. The justification gap – justified false belief has no home. 
A belief can be properly justified and still be false; JTB is factive so it is not K. With only K/B the justified false belief J&¬T&B is forced into mere Belief and is lumped with unjustified false belief ¬J&¬T&B. The epistemic virtue of justification is invisible once truth fails: a rational, well grounded false belief is indiscriminable from an arbitrary, irrational false belief. Knowledge is thereby too narrow and Belief is made too broad.

2. The truth gap – unjustified true belief has no home. 
A belief can be true by luck, accident or blind guess with no justification at all; JTB is justification dependent so it is not K. With only K/B the unjustified true belief ¬J&T&B is forced into mere Belief and is lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is invisible once justification fails: a lucky true belief is indiscriminable from a false belief. Belief therefore conflates epistemically good justification/bad truth with bad justification/good truth.

That is the classic coarse-graining objection, distinct from Gettier. It is the formal expression of the regress/dogmatism worry colleagues 10-11 raise: J cannot be cashed out in B/K terms without making justification either regress ad infinitum through B-states or stop arbitrarily in a basic K/B, i.e. you have no independent state for “justified belief” as such. The upshot is that on a bare Knowledge/Belief inventory JTB cannot keep apart warranted error from unwarranted error, nor lucky truth from warranted truth.

With only K = J & T & B and B = ¬K in the inventory the 2x2 J/T matrix
collapses into one positive cell and one heterogeneous residual.

* J T B = Knowledge
* J ~T B = Belief
* ~J T B = Belief
* ~J ~T B = Belief

Belief is therefore J&~T&B ∨ ~J&T&B ∨ ~J&~T&B. Justification and truth can
no longer be tracked independently of the K/B dichotomy.

1. The justification gap / justified-false-belief gap.  
A belief can be properly justified and still false. On JTB it is not
Knowledge because the truth condition fails, so on a K/B only taxonomy it
must be counted as mere Belief. Justified false belief is thereby lumped
together with unjustified false belief. The epistemic value of being
justified is erased once truth fails and there is no epistemic home for
‘justified belief as such’. Justified falsity is epistemically indiscriminable
from unjustified falsity.

2. The truth gap / unjustified-true-belief gap.  
A belief can be true by luck, accident or blind guess and yet be wholly
unjustified. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the justification condition
fails, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must again be counted as mere Belief.
Unjustified true belief is thereby lumped together with justified false
belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic value of being true is
erased once justification fails and there is no epistemic home for ‘true
belief as such’. Lucky truth is epistemically indiscriminable from false
belief.

it is expressed as the fact that with no distinct justified-belief state
justification has nowhere to be realised except via further B or K states.
Cashing J(p) out by B(q) generates the regress of justification, and cashing

regress / circularity and the truth-verification worry are just the
meta-epistemic expression of the same inventory limit: justification cannot
be marked off from belief when truth is absent and truth cannot be marked
off from belief when justification is absent.

* J ∧ T ∧ B = K
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = Belief

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag and the
justification / truth matrix is coarse-grained to Knowledge vs not-Knowledge.

The two cells that are lost are the two non-K cells that are epistemically
distinct from plain unwarranted false belief.

properly justified and yet false. JTB is factive so J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not K.
With only K/B as states it must be counted as mere Belief, and is lumped
together with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The epistemic virtue of justification is
erased once truth fails: a well warranted false belief is
indistinguishable in the taxonomy from an arbitrary, unjustified false

2. The truth gap / unjustified-true-belief problem. A belief can be true
by luck, accident or blind guess with no justification at all. JTB is
justification dependent so ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not K. With only K/B as states
it must again be counted as mere Belief, and is lumped together both with

taxonomy from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false

With only two labels, K and B, the JxT space is forced to coarse grain.

On JTB
K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p)

and everything else is just B. On a binary inventory

* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = Belief

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the residual category. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction of justified false, true unjustified and unjustified false belief.

That coarse graining makes two intuitively distinct non-knowledge states disappear.

1. The justification gap / justified false belief. 
J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is factive. With K/B only it must be counted as mere Belief. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore lumped with an arbitrary, unjustified false belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth is absent: justified falsity and unjustified falsity are indiscriminable as mere belief, even though the former is epistemically much better than the latter. In the taxonomy there is no place for a justified belief as such.

2. The truth gap / unjustified true belief. 
¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is justification dependent. With K/B only it must be counted as mere Belief. A lucky, accidental or blindly guessed true belief is therefore lumped with justified false belief and with unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification is absent: accidentally true belief is indiscriminable as mere belief from false belief, even though it shares truth with knowledge and is alethically better than false belief. In the taxonomy there is no place for a true belief as such.

Hence Knowledge is too narrow and Belief is too broad. Belief has to do duty for both “justified but false” and “true but unjustified”. The formal expression of the loss is the classic regress/circularity of the J-clause on a B/K only stock: J(p) can only be cashed out by another B or K state, so J(p) either needs J(q) ad infinitum if cashed out by belief, or requires K(q) which already contains a belief needing a justifier, i.e. circularity/dogmatism. The regress/circularity is the formal consequence of having no independent justified-belief state to realise justification, and the JFB / UTB collapse is the observable taxonomy consequence.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion has converged on the coarse-graining consequence of restricting the epistemic inventory to Knowledge and Belief, with the regress/circularity worry now mainly treated as the formal expression of that coarse-graining rather than an independent problem.

With K(p):=B(p)&T(p)&J(p) and only K/B labels available, B is the residual ¬K. That forces

K = J∧T∧B
B = J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B

so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag.

Dominant account, Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12,14 and now Colleague 1 in round 1:
1. Justification gap / justified false belief problem. J∧¬T∧B is not K because JTB is factive. On K/B only it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧T∧B. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails; there is no epistemic place for ‘justified belief as such’ or for ‘justified but wrong’. Knowledge is too narrow, Belief is too broad.
2. Truth gap / unjustified true belief problem. ¬J∧T∧B is not K because JTB is justification dependent. On K/B only it must also be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails; there is no epistemic place for ‘true belief as such’ or for ‘true but unwarranted’. Lucky truth is indiscriminable from false belief.

Most colleagues now frame the regress/circularity worry as downstream of the inventory limit. J(p) must be cashed out in the only available states. Cashing it out via B(q) yields J(q) → infinite regress of beliefs each needing a justifier. Cashing it out via K(q) reintroduces J(q) since K(q)=B(q)&T(q)&J(q), giving circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational stop. That is the formal way the lack of an independent justified-belief state makes justification unstatable on a bare K/B stock, and it is why the two non-knowledge cells JFB and UTB have no home.

Minor residual strand: Colleagues 1,5,7,9,10,11,13,14 still mention truth-verification without presupposing knowledge and the need for a non-arbitrary stopping point for justification. The group now largely treats those as the meta-epistemic expression of the same coarse-graining, and as blockable by externalist/foundational moves, not distinctive to JTB under the two-state constraint.

Unresolved / still live: phrasing of the two problems as “regress/circularity + non-verifiability of truth” vs “loss of distinct places for JFB and UTB”. The operative consensus in round 1 is that the latter is the primary taxonomic defect and the former is its formal consequence; Gettier remains explicitly set aside.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB analysis under a strict K/B inventory is now converging on the coarse-graining/oblivion of independent J and T tracking as the non-Gettier pressure.

Consensus core:
K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p). With only K and B as attitude kinds, ¬K is forced into a single residual B. Hence
K = J∧T∧B
B = J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B
Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside Belief. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag.

The two observable gaps that dominate the current round:
1. Justification gap / justified false belief. J∧¬T∧B is not K because JTB is factive, so on K/B only it must be counted as mere Belief. Properly warranted but false belief is therefore lumped with ¬J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧T∧B. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails; there is no state for justified belief as such, and rational error is indiscriminable from irrational error.
2. Truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J∧T∧B is not K because JTB is justification dependent, so on K/B only it must also be counted as mere Belief. Lucky/accidental/ blind-guess true belief is lumped with J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails; there is no state for true belief as such, and lucky truth is indiscriminable from false belief.

Knowledge is therefore too narrow – it excludes justified false beliefs we want as epistemically good – and Belief is too broad – it conflates warranted error with unwarranted error and lucky truth with falsehood.

Secondary/derivative strand:
Several colleagues 10,11 still frame the problem as a regress/circularity/dogmatism dilemma for J(p): J(p) must be cashed out in epistemic terms, i.e. in B(q) or K(q). B(q) → J(q) gives infinite regress; K(q) := B(q)&T(q)&J(q) re-introduces J(q) and yields circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational stop. The regress/circularity is now widely treated in the current round as the formal expression of why justification cannot be realized as an independent state on a bare K/B inventory, not as a separate pair of problems. Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9 argue it is derivative: the taxonomy loss is primary, the regress only surfaces once one tries to cash J out inside the already collapsed space. Colleague 7 proposes a hybrid: the collapse is primary and the truth-checking regress is downstream.

Changes from previous reflection:
I was keeping both the JFB/UTB collapse and the regress/circularity as co-equal candidates. Current round weight strongly favours JFB and UTB as the two intended problems; regress/circularity is best understood as the meta-epistemic mechanism that explains why the inventory cannot host an independent justified-belief state.

Unresolved:
Whether the exam expects the two problems phrased strictly as “justified false belief has no home / unjustified true belief has no home” or as “justification gap and truth gap” / “regress vs circularity”. Majority textual weight in rounds 0-1 favours the first pair; the regress framing is now seen as explanatory rather than the two distinct problems themselves. Gettier is explicitly set aside.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The inventory restriction to Knowledge = J ∧ T ∧ B and Belief as the sole residual class forces a coarse-graining of the 2×2 J×T matrix.

With K/B only:
* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = Belief

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous disjunction and J and T can no longer be tracked independently inside it.

The stable core that emerges across rounds 0-1 is the loss of two non-Gettier cells that become indistinguishable from plain unwarranted false belief.

1. Justification gap / justified false belief. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is factive, so on a K/B taxonomy it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore indistinguishable from an arbitrary unjustified false belief; the epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails. Knowledge is too narrow and there is no epistemic place for justified belief as such.

2. Truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is justification dependent, so on a K/B taxonomy it must also be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A lucky/accidental true belief is therefore indistinguishable from justified false belief and from unjustified false belief; the alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails. There is no epistemic place for true belief as such.

Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,12 repeatedly formalise this as the JFB and UTB collapse; Colleagues 1,10,11,5,7,9,14 frame it as the formal impossibility of cashing out J(p) in the only available states. The two framings are compatible: because there is no independent justified-belief state, J(p) must be given in B/K terms.

* If J(p) is cashed out by B(q), J(q) is required, etc., giving the familiar regress of justification.
* If the chain is stopped by K(q), K(q) := B(q)∧T(q)∧J(q) re-introduces a belief needing a justifier, yielding circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational basic belief/knowledge.

Current round 1 discussion strengthens the taxonomy reading. Colleagues 13,14,5,7 argue regress/circularity is derivative/downstream of the already-collapsed K/B space and that externalist/foundational stops can block a practical regress but cannot restore the lost JFB/UTB distinctions. Colleagues 10,11 continue to stress regress/circularity as the formal expression of the coarse-graining.

Unresolved wording: whether the question wants the two problems stated as “justified false belief vs unjustified false belief” and “unjustified true belief vs false belief” coarse-graining, or as “regress/circularity of justification” and “inability to verify truth non-circularly”. Current weight of evidence favours the JFB and UTB coarse-graining as the canonical non-Gettier problems, with regress/circularity as the underlying justification problem that explains why the inventory cannot support an independent justified-belief state.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains centred on the collapse of the J/T matrix when the epistemic inventory is restricted to Knowledge and Belief with K(p):=B(p)&T(p)&J(p). With only K/B, every non-K attitude is forced into the residual Belief class, i.e. Belief ≡ J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B. Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside Belief.

The dominant consensus across round 0 and round 1 is the coarse-graining / independence loss, expressed as two lost non-knowledge cells:

* Justification gap / justified false belief. J∧¬T∧B is not K because K is factive. On a K/B only scheme it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧¬T∧B. The epistemic virtue of justification is invisible once truth fails; there is no taxonomic place for a warranted but false belief, so justified falsity is indiscriminable from unjustified falsity. Knowledge is too narrow, Belief too broad.

* Truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J∧T∧B is not K because K requires justification. On a K/B only scheme it is also forced into mere Belief and is lumped with J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. The alethic virtue of truth is invisible once justification fails; a lucky/accidental true belief is indiscriminable from false belief. There is no taxonomic place for true belief as such.

These two gaps are the observable taxonomy consequence of the JTB restriction.

A second strand, raised strongly by colleagues 10,11, and echoed in 2,4,6,8,12, is the formal justification problem: J(p) has to be cashed out in the only available states B or K. Cashing it out by B(q) yields an infinite regress J(p)→B(q)→J(q)→…; stopping by K(q) re-introduces J(q) because K(q):=B(q)&T(q)&J(q), giving circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary basic belief/knowledge stop. Colleague 7/13 note externalist/foundational stops can block regress in practice but cannot restore the lost JFB/UTB distinctions.

Remaining nuance: some colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 also mention difficulty verifying truth and specifying a non-arbitrary justification standard from within K/B only, which is a variant of the grounding worry.

Unresolved for me: whether the question wants the two state-collapse cases or the two justificatory structural problems of regress vs dogmatism/circularity. The weight of evidence in round 1 leans to the former as the intended two problems – no epistemic place for justified false belief and no epistemic place for unjustified true belief – with regress/circularity as the formal meta-epistemic expression of that same inventory limit. Gettier is set aside.

reflection_text.10:

K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p). With only K and B as attitude kinds, ¬K is forced into a single residual B. Hence
K = J∧T∧B
B = J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B
Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside Belief. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag.

The two observable gaps that dominate the current round:

reflection_text.12:
The inventory restriction to Knowledge = J ∧ T ∧ B and Belief as the sole residual class forces a coarse-graining of the 2×2 J×T matrix.

With K/B only:
* J ∧ T ∧ B = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = Belief

The stable core that emerges across rounds 0-1 is the loss of two non-Gettier cells that become indistinguishable from plain unwarranted false belief.

1. Justification gap / justified false belief. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is factive, so on a K/B taxonomy it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore indistinguishable from an arbitrary unjustified false belief; the epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails. Knowledge is too narrow and there is no epistemic place for justified belief as such.

2. Truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because JTB is justification dependent, so on a K/B taxonomy it must also be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A lucky/accidental true belief is therefore indistinguishable from justified false belief and from unjustified false belief; the alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails. * If the chain is stopped by K(q), K(q) := B(q)∧T(q)∧J(q) re-introduces a belief needing a justifier, yielding circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational basic belief/knowledge.

reflection_text.11:

* Justification gap / justified false belief. J∧¬T∧B is not K because K is factive. On a K/B only scheme it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧¬T∧B. The epistemic virtue of justification is invisible once truth fails; there is no taxonomic place for a warranted but false belief, so justified falsity is indiscriminable from unjustified falsity. Knowledge is too narrow, Belief too broad.

* Truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J∧T∧B is not K because K requires justification. On a K/B only scheme it is also forced into mere Belief and is lumped with J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. The alethic virtue of truth is invisible once justification fails; a lucky/accidental true belief is indiscriminable from false belief. There is no taxonomic place for true belief as such.

Cashing it out by B(q) yields an infinite regress J(p)→B(q)→J(q)→…; stopping by K(q) re-introduces J(q) because K(q):=B(q)&T(q)&J(q), giving circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary basic belief/knowledge stop. Unresolved for me: whether the question wants the two state-collapse cases or the two justificatory structural problems of regress vs dogmatism/circularity. The weight of evidence in round 1 leans to the former as the intended two problems – no epistemic place for justified false belief and no epistemic place for unjustified true belief – with regress/circularity as the formal meta-epistemic expression of that same inventory limit. 14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 13, 14, 5, 7 and 9 have already isolated the decisive point: once the taxonomy is restricted to Knowledge and Belief alone, the four cells of the J × T matrix are collapsed into a single residual label, so that J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ T ∧ B become indistinguishable from every other non-K state. That loss of independent tracking is not a downstream consequence of an attempted regress; it is the immediate structural result of the two-state constraint itself. Any subsequent attempt to restore an independent role for J by cashing it out in further B or K states simply reproduces the same two gaps inside the already-coarsened category, because the justifier must again be either Knowledge (which is factive and justification-dependent) or Belief (which is already heterogeneous). The heterogeneity of Belief and the erasure of the justification gap and truth gap therefore remain the primary defects that JTB exhibits under the given inventory, even before any chain of further beliefs is considered.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 10 and 11 rightly note that cashing out J(p) under a strict K/B inventory quickly produces regress or circularity, yet that worry is not the primary defect imposed by the constraint itself. Externalist or foundational stopping points—whether reliabilist mechanisms or basic non-inferential states—can truncate any actual chain without contradiction, leaving the J-clause satisfiable in practice. What cannot be rescued by such stops is the forced taxonomy: with only Knowledge and Belief available, the four cells of the J/T matrix collapse so that J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧T∧B are both dumped into the single residual label Belief. This erases any capacity to mark justification when truth fails or truth when justification fails, rendering JTB unable to preserve the intended normative distinctions even after the regress is blocked. The heterogeneity of Belief therefore remains the more fundamental and distinctive problem once Gettier cases are set aside.

* B = J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B

Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class. Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag and two epistemically distinct non-knowledge cells disappear.

1. The justification gap / justified-false-belief problem. JTB is factive. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not K, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and with ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore indistinguishable in the taxonomy from an arbitrary unjustified false belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails; there is no independent state for justified belief as such, and Knowledge is too narrow because it excludes justified false beliefs we want to count as epistemically good.

2. The truth gap / unjustified-true-belief problem. JTB is justification dependent. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not K, so on a K/B only taxonomy it must also be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A lucky, accidental or blindly guessed true belief is therefore indistinguishable in the taxonomy from justified false belief and from unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails; there is no independent state for true belief as such, and Belief is too broad because it conflates lucky truth with falsehood.

That coarse-graining is the formal expression of why J cannot be cashed out on a bare K/B stock without regress/circularity. J(p) has to be given in the only available states, so J(p) is cashed out by B(q) → J(q) ad infinitum, or by K(q) := B(q)&T(q)&J(q) which re-introduces J(q) and gives circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational stop. The regress/dogmatism worry is therefore downstream of the inventory limit: there is no independent justified-belief state to realise justification, which is why JFB and UTB have no home. Gettier aside, this is the classic truth-versus-justification pressure on JTB under a two-state restriction.

12.text:
With only K and B as live labels the J×T matrix is forced to coarse-grain to K vs ¬K.

K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p)
¬K(p) := B(p) & [¬T(p) ∨ ¬J(p)]

i.e.

* J∧T∧B = Knowledge
* J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B = Belief

Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class. Belief becomes the heterogeneous disjunction of justified false, true unjustified and unjustified false belief. That is the inventory loss that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12 make explicit.

The two non-Gettier cells that disappear are:

1. The justification gap / justified false belief problem.
J∧¬T∧B is not Knowledge because JTB is factive. On a K/B only taxonomy it must be classed as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J∧¬T∧B. A properly warranted but false belief is therefore indistinguishable in the taxonomy from an arbitrary, unjustified false belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails: there is no epistemic place for justified belief as such, and Knowledge is too narrow because it excludes justified false beliefs we want to count as epistemically good. Belief is made too broad by conflating warranted error with unwarranted error.

2. The truth gap / unjustified true belief problem.
¬J∧T∧B is not Knowledge because JTB is justification dependent. On a K/B only taxonomy it must also be classed as mere Belief and is lumped with J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. A lucky, accidental or blindly guessed true belief is therefore indistinguishable in the taxonomy from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails: there is no epistemic place for true belief as such. Belief therefore conflates epistemically good justification/bad truth with bad justification/good truth.

That coarse-graining is the formal expression of why J(p) cannot be realised on a bare K/B inventory. J(p) has to be cashed out in epistemic terms as a further B(q) or K(q). Cashing it out by B(q) gives the familiar regress J(p)→B(q)→J(q)→..., and closing the chain by K(q) re-introduces J(q) because K(q):=B(q)&T(q)&J(q), i.e. circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational basic belief/knowledge. The regress/circularity worry is derivative: it is the meta-epistemic form of the already collapsed JFB/UTB space. Even with externalist or foundational stops the taxonomy remains unable to mark warranted error off from unwarranted error, nor lucky truth off from warranted truth.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB inventory under the strict K/B restriction is stable and converging.

K(p) := B(p) & T(p) & J(p). With only Knowledge and Belief as attitude labels, ¬K is forced to be the single residual class
K = J ∧ T ∧ B
Belief ≡ ¬K ≡ J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B

The 2×2 Justified/Unjustified × True/False matrix is coarse-grained to Knowledge vs not-Knowledge. Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside the Belief class; Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag and Knowledge is too narrow, Belief too broad.

The two observable non-Gettier losses that are now dominant in the group are:

* Justification gap / justified false belief. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not K because JTB is factive. On a K/B only taxonomy it must be counted as mere Belief and is lumped with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. A properly warranted but false belief is taxonomically indistinguishable from an arbitrary unjustified false belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is erased once truth fails: there is no state for ‘justified belief as such’. Knowledge excludes justified false beliefs we want as epistemically good; Belief conflates warranted error with unwarranted error.

* Truth gap / unjustified true belief. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not K because JTB is justification dependent. On a K/B only taxonomy it is also forced into mere Belief and is lumped with J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A lucky, accidental or blind-guess true belief is taxonomically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is erased once justification fails: there is no state for ‘true belief as such’. Belief conflates lucky truth with falsehood.

Regress / circularity / external verification is the mechanism many colleagues invoke for why the collapse is unavoidable on a bare K/B stock. J(p) must be cashed out in the only available states: via B(q) → J(p)→B(q)→J(q)→... infinite regress of beliefs each needing a justifier; via K(q)→K(q) already contains B(q)&J(q) so justification of p depends on justification of q → circularity/dogmatism or an arbitrary foundational stop.

Round 3 convergence: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12,13,14 now describe the same coarse-graining and name the two gaps as justification gap / JFB and truth gap / UTB. Colleagues 1,13,14,5,7,9,2,3,4,6,8 argue regress/circularity is real but derivative: it surfaces only if one still attempts to analyse J inside the already-collapsed K/B space; externalist or foundational stops can truncate an actual chain without restoring the lost distinctions. Colleagues 10,11 continue to foreground regress/circularity as co-constitutive, but frame it as the formal expression of the taxonomy loss.

My current leaning remains with the majority thread: the intended non-Gettier difficulties under a strict K/B inventory are the inability to keep justification and truth independently trackable, i.e. the forced conflation of justified false belief with mere belief and of unjustified true belief with mere belief. Regress/circularity is the meta-epistemic expression of the same inventory limit, not a second independent observable problem. Gettier is to be ignored. The earlier unresolved wording tension J¬T/¬JT vs justification gap/truth gap has settled in practice on the gap terminology with the explicit cell references retained.
